questions.question_text: A closed cylinder has a radius of $6$ cm and a height of $4$ cm. Find its surface area in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Counts only one circular end ($\pi r^{2}$) instead of two ($2\pi r^{2}$).
Gives only the curved surface $2\pi rh$ and omits the two circular ends.
Uses $\pi rh$ for the curved surface, halving the correct $2\pi rh$.

questions.question_text: A closed cylinder has a radius of $3$ cm and a height of $14$ cm. Find its surface area, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Counts only one circular end instead of two, losing one $\pi r^{2}$.
Gives only the curved surface $2\pi rh$ and leaves out both ends.

questions.question_text: A closed cylinder has a diameter of $12$ cm and a height of $7$ cm. Find its surface area in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Uses the diameter $12$ as the radius instead of halving it to $6$.
Counts only one circular end instead of two circular ends.
Gives only the curved surface $2\pi rh$ and omits both ends.

questions.question_text: A drink can is modelled as a closed cylinder of radius $2.5$ cm and height $9$ cm. Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Counts only one circular end, dropping one $\pi r^{2}$ term.
Gives only the curved surface $2\pi rh$ and leaves out both ends.

questions.question_text: Which expression gives the total surface area of a closed cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$?

options.why: Includes only one circular end, but a closed cylinder has two ends.
Halves the curved surface; the curved rectangle is $2\pi rh$, not $\pi rh$.
Gives only the curved surface and omits the two circular ends.

questions.solution_text:
A closed cylinder has two circular ends of total area $2\pi r^{2}$ and a curved surface of area $2\pi rh$.
$A = 2\pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$

questions.question_text: A closed cylinder has a radius of $4$ cm, and its curved surface area is $96\pi$ cm². Find the height of the cylinder.

options.why: Treats $96\pi$ as the total surface area, subtracting the two ends first.
Uses $\pi rh$ instead of $2\pi rh$ for the curved surface, halving the divisor.

questions.question_text: A closed cylinder has a height equal to twice its radius. Its total surface area is $54\pi$ cm². Find the radius.

options.why: Stops at $r^{2} = 9$ without taking the square root to find $r$.
Reports the height $2r = 6$ instead of the radius that was asked for.

questions.question_text: A closed cylindrical tank has a diameter of $1.8$ m and a height of $2.5$ m. Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Uses the diameter $1.8$ as the radius instead of halving it to $0.9$.
Gives only the curved surface $2\pi rh$ and omits both ends.

questions.question_text: A closed cylinder has a radius of $3$ m and a total surface area of $200$ m². Find its height, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Uses only the curved surface $2\pi rh = 200$, ignoring the two ends.
Subtracts only one circular end instead of two before dividing.
